$ xref card

by Alexander Panasenko · xrefcode.com
On this page
  1. Usage
  2. Arguments and options

A one-screen summary of a function: which argument registers and stack slots it reads, its return registers, the fields it stores to (grouped by base), every call with its decoded arguments, indirect calls, panic paths and exits. Use it to decide whether a function is worth reading in full with c.

Usage

xref card [OPTIONS] <FN>

Arguments and options

Arguments

<FN>
Target function address or symbol name.

Options

--json
Emit the function card as JSON.

Examples

Summarize a function

ripgrep's statistics serializer (see field):

Command
$ xref -b rg card 0x1835f0
Output
function 0x1835f0..0x18374c
inputs:
  registers: rdi, rsi
  stack: none
return registers: rax
stores:
  arg1:
    +0x18: 8
    +0x20: 1
  stack:
    +0x0: 8
    +0x8: 1
callees:
  0x183644: 0x15bf60(rdi=rsp, rsi=0x492c0b ("elapsedsearchessearches_with_matchbytes_searchedbytes_printedmat"), rdx=7, rcx=rcx (dynamic), stack0=rsi (dynamic), stack1=1)
  0x183664: 0x158e60(rdi=rsp, rsi=0x492c12 ("searchessearches_with_matchbytes_searchedbytes_printedmatched_li"), rdx=8, rcx=rbx, stack0=rsi (dynamic), stack1=1)
  0x183685: 0x158e60(rdi=rsp, rsi=0x492c1a ("searches_with_matchbytes_searchedbytes_printedmatched_linesmatch"), rdx=0x13, rcx=rcx (dynamic), stack0=rsi (dynamic), stack1=1)
  0x1836a6: 0x158e60(rdi=rsp, rsi=0x492c2d ("bytes_searchedbytes_printedmatched_linesmatchesbeginendmatchcont"), rdx=0xe, rcx=rcx (dynamic), stack0=rsi (dynamic), stack1=1)
  0x1836c3: 0x158e60(rdi=rsp, rsi=0x492c3b ("bytes_printedmatched_linesmatchesbeginendmatchcontextstartnanosh"), rdx=0xd, rcx=rcx (dynamic), stack0=rsi (dynamic), stack1=1)
  0x1836e0: 0x158e60(rdi=rsp, rsi=0x492c48 ("matched_linesmatchesbeginendmatchcontextstartnanoshumanPoisonErr"), rdx=0xd, rcx=rcx (dynamic), stack0=rsi (dynamic), stack1=1)
  0x183700: 0x158e60(rdi=rsp, rsi=0x492c55 ("matchesbeginendmatchcontextstartnanoshumanPoisonError"), rdx=7, rcx=rbx, stack0=rsi (dynamic), stack1=1)
  0x183712: 0x187760(rdi=u64 [rsp], rsi=u32 [rsp+0x8], stack0=rsi (dynamic), stack1=1)

stderr
xref: load 2.4ms, total 5.2ms

How to read it:

  • inputs: argument registers and stack arguments the function reads before writing them.
  • stores: memory written, grouped by base (arg1 is the second argument, rsi); each line is an offset and the store widths in bytes.
  • callees: each call site, its target and the arguments xref could decode. A string argument shows the address and a preview of the bytes there; the length argument (rdx=8 for searches) says how many of them belong to the string, the rest of the preview is whatever follows in .rodata. (dynamic) marks values computed at run time.
  • panics and exits: panic call sites and return instructions.

Machine-readable

Command
$ xref -b rg card 0x1835f0 --json
Output
{
  "function": {
    "start": 1586672,
    "end": 1587020,
    "name": null
  },
  "inputs": {
    "registers": [
      "rdi",
      "rsi"
    ],
    "stack_args": []
  },
  "return_registers": [
    "rax"
  ],
  "stores": {
    "arg1": [
      {
        "offset": 24,
        "widths": [
          8
        ]
      },
      {
        "offset": 32,
        "widths": [
          1
        ]
      }
Output cut here: lines 1–30 of 177 shown.
stderr
xref: load 2.5ms, total 5.2ms

Limits

  • Argument decoding follows the x86-64 System V convention; values passed through memory or computed in callers show as (dynamic).
  • stack0, stack1 are the first stack-passed argument slots at the call site as the decoder sees them; for calls with six or fewer register arguments they may hold unrelated values.

Provenance

Recorded with a development build of xref after 0.4.0 on Linux x86-64, on rg = ripgrep 14.1.1 (official stripped release). Output is unchanged; long outputs are cut where marked. <!-- /xref -->
